# Backtest results — XAUUSD liquidity-sweep model

*Generated by `node report.js` on 2026-08-04 18:42 UTC. Every figure is recomputed from the data files on each run — edit the data, not this document.*

---

## Bottom line

The model produces **few trades with a high win rate on the data available, and that result does not survive out-of-sample testing on the 4-hour set.** The per-trade tables below look encouraging in isolation; the robustness section explains why they should not yet be trusted. The binding constraint is not the strategy's accuracy but how rarely it fires, which keeps every sample too small to draw a conclusion from.

Read the per-dataset sections for what happened, then the robustness section for whether it means anything.

---

## Pooled cross-market test

Every dataset below was run on **identical parameters** (the config defaults — `pivotLen=5, confirmBars=6, rr=2, requireFVG=true, requirePD=true`). Nothing was tuned per market. Each market is therefore out-of-sample with respect to every other, and pooling the trades builds the larger sample that no single market can provide.

### Per-market results

| Market | Timeframe | Bars | Span | Signals | Trades | Win rate | Total R | Expectancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gold | daily | 800 | 1132d | 5 | 5 | 0% | -5.03R | -1.01R |
| Gold | 4-hour | 671 | 137d | 6 | 5 | 80% | +6.95R | +1.39R |
| Gold | 1-hour | 902 | 56d | 8 | 7 | 57% | +4.85R | +0.69R |
| Gold | 15-minute | 801 | 13d | 8 | 8 | 25% | -2.32R | -0.29R |
| Silver | 1-hour | 801 | 49d | 6 | 6 | 33% | -3.77R | -0.63R |
| Tesla | 1-hour | 701 | 146d | 5 | 5 | 40% | +0.74R | +0.15R |
| Reddit | 1-hour | 862 | 180d | 8 | 8 | 0% | -8.56R | -1.07R |
| **Pooled** | — | 5538 | — | — | **44** | **32%** | **-7.14R** | **-0.16R** |

### Verdict

| | |
|---|---|
| Pooled trades | 44 |
| Win rate | 32% |
| Expectancy | -0.16R per trade |
| 95% confidence interval | -0.59R to 0.26R |
| Markets with positive expectancy | 3 of 7 |

> **The pooled confidence interval still straddles zero** (-0.59R to 0.26R). Even with 44 trades across 4 instruments, this sample cannot distinguish the model from chance. The direction is discouraging, but it is not yet evidence.

## Robustness: does the edge survive?

A backtest run over the same data used to choose the settings will almost always look profitable. Two checks guard against that: a full parameter sweep, to see whether the result depends on one lucky configuration, and a walk-forward split, to see whether settings chosen on past data still work on data they have never seen.

### XAUUSD daily

Grid of **960 parameter combinations** over `pivotLen`, `confirmBars`, `rr`, `maxRiskATR`, `requireFVG` and `requirePD`, each backtested over the full file.

| | |
|---|---|
| Combinations tested | 960 |
| Clearing the 8-trade floor | 280 |
| ...of those, positive expectancy | 134 (48%) |
| ...of those, 95% CI entirely above zero | 0 |

**Walk-forward.** Parameters chosen using only the first half of the data, then applied unchanged to the second half. This is the only test here that answers "would this have made money going forward".

| | In-sample (first half) | Out-of-sample (second half) |
|---|---|---|
| Period | 2023-06-28 22:00 → 2025-01-14 23:00 | 2025-01-15 23:00 → 2026-08-03 22:00 |
| Bars | 400 | 400 |
| Best config expectancy | +0.99R (4 trades) | +0.14R (7 trades) |
| Top-decile mean expectancy | +0.64R | +0.05R |
| Top-decile configs still profitable | 10/10 | 6/10 |

Best in-sample configuration: `pivotLen=3 confirmBars=10 rr=3 maxRiskATR=0 requireFVG=true requirePD=false`

**Decay: 0.589R lost** moving from fitted data to unseen data.

### XAUUSD 4-hour

Grid of **960 parameter combinations** over `pivotLen`, `confirmBars`, `rr`, `maxRiskATR`, `requireFVG` and `requirePD`, each backtested over the full file.

| | |
|---|---|
| Combinations tested | 960 |
| Clearing the 8-trade floor | 323 |
| ...of those, positive expectancy | 310 (96%) |
| ...of those, 95% CI entirely above zero | 2 |

> When **96% of all settings look profitable**, the result is measuring the sample, not the settings. A genuine edge is selective; noise is generous.

**Walk-forward.** Parameters chosen using only the first half of the data, then applied unchanged to the second half. This is the only test here that answers "would this have made money going forward".

| | In-sample (first half) | Out-of-sample (second half) |
|---|---|---|
| Period | 2026-03-20 08:00 → 2026-05-28 08:00 | 2026-05-28 12:00 → 2026-08-04 16:00 |
| Bars | 335 | 336 |
| Best config expectancy | +1.99R (4 trades) | **no trades at all** |
| Top-decile mean expectancy | +1.68R | -1.01R |
| Top-decile configs still profitable | 49/49 | 0/28 |

Best in-sample configuration: `pivotLen=6 confirmBars=6 rr=2 maxRiskATR=0 requireFVG=true requirePD=true`

**Decay: 2.696R lost** moving from fitted data to unseen data.

> The top decile was profitable in-sample and **loses money out-of-sample**, with 28 of 28 configurations failing. This is the signature of fitting noise: the parameters learned this particular stretch of history rather than anything that repeats.

## Data ceiling

The datasets above are small, and that is a limit of the data source rather than a choice.

- The IBKR `get_price_history` endpoint refuses any request resolving to more than **3,500 data points**.
- It accepts a `period` or a `step_count`, but **no start date**. Every response ends at the present moment, so history cannot be paged backwards — there is no way to ask for an earlier window.
- In practice the binding limit is tighter still: responses above roughly 25,000 tokens are rejected and spilled to a file unreachable from the sandbox, capping a single retrieval at a few hundred bars.

**Consequence.** At roughly one signal per 120 bars, a full year of 1-hour data would still yield only about 65 trades. Reaching the 100+ trades needed for a statistically meaningful verdict requires 2–3 years of 1-hour history, which means fetching from IBKR directly to disk rather than through this route.

---

## Method

**Costs.** Every trade is charged 0.3 points of spread once on entry and 0.2 points of slippage on both entry and exit.

**Ambiguous bars count as losses.** When a single bar's range contains both the stop and the target, bar data cannot say which was touched first, so the trade is recorded as a loss. This understates performance on wide-target settings — deliberately, because the opposite assumption is how backtests end up lying.

**Unresolved signals are excluded.** A signal still open when the data ends is not counted as a win or a loss.

**Percentages are instrument moves,** not account returns: the change in the price of gold between entry and exit after costs. Position sizing is a separate decision.

### Reproducing every number here

```bash
node test.js                                        # 38 unit tests
node verify-data.js                                 # data integrity + regenerate manifest
node backtest.js data/xauusd-1d.json                # XAUUSD daily summary
node backtest.js data/xauusd-4h.json                # XAUUSD 4-hour summary
node backtest.js data/xauusd-1h.json                # XAUUSD 1-hour summary
node backtest.js data/xauusd-15m.json               # XAUUSD 15-minute summary
node backtest.js data/xagusd-1h.json                # XAGUSD 1-hour summary
node backtest.js data/tsla-1h.json                  # TSLA 1-hour summary
node backtest.js data/rddt-1h.json                  # RDDT 1-hour summary
node sweep.js data/xauusd-1d.json 8                 # XAUUSD daily sweep + walk-forward
node sweep.js data/xauusd-4h.json 8                 # XAUUSD 4-hour sweep + walk-forward
node sweep.js data/xauusd-1h.json 10                # XAUUSD 1-hour sweep + walk-forward
node sweep.js data/xauusd-15m.json 10               # XAUUSD 15-minute sweep + walk-forward
node sweep.js data/xagusd-1h.json 10                # XAGUSD 1-hour sweep + walk-forward
node sweep.js data/tsla-1h.json 10                  # TSLA 1-hour sweep + walk-forward
node sweep.js data/rddt-1h.json 10                  # RDDT 1-hour sweep + walk-forward
node report.js                                      # regenerate this document
```

### Data provenance

Both files are verbatim `get_price_history` responses for contract `69067924` (XAUUSD, "London Gold", IBCMDTY), MidPoint source, `outside_rth=true`. Each was verified against an independent re-fetch: all closed bars matched exactly, with no inverted bars, no outlier gaps, and correct bar spacing.
